scope: How each KNOWLEDGE-relevant generator would consume the canonical model — not a rewrite plan. 'currentDatasetReads' is verified against source (Phase 1A/1B/1C tracing); 'canonicalFieldsRequired' is what that generator would read from a single Name Entity record instead, under the model in schemas/name-entity.schema.json.
outOfScopeNote: Non-knowledge-rendering scripts (index-integrity-audit.js, sitemap-hygiene-report.js, origin-integrity-audit.js, crawl-depth-distribution.js, internal-link-density-report.js, topic-cluster-map.js, minify-css.js, and the other ~50 audit/utility/build scripts cataloged in audit/build-pipeline.json) are excluded — they check or transform build output rather than render canonical knowledge into a page, so they have no canonical-field dependency to map.

generators.role: Page-generation (master generator — name-detail, names-like, letter/gender/country/style, last-name filter, compatibility, root hub pages)
generators.note: The single largest consumer — would read nearly every domain of the canonical model. This is the generator that currently reads the enriched file correctly.

generators.role: Page-generation (standalone Names Like runner; same logic embedded in generate-programmatic-pages.js)
generators.note: Note this standalone script reads data/names.json (unenriched), while generate-programmatic-pages.js's embedded copy of the same logic reads data/names-enriched.json — an internal inconsistency between two implementations of the same page. Confirmed via source in this phase; see audit/knowledge-redundancy.json.

The generator behind the Phase 1C/1D headline finding: reads data/names.json instead of data/names-enriched.json, so origin.cluster is unavailable to it even for names where the canonical record would have a real value. Under the canonical model, this generator would read the SAME entity record as every other generator, structurally eliminating this gap.

canonicalFieldsRequired: identity.* (of the first names being matched)
(Surname Entity fields — out of scope for this schema)
generators.note: The one generator whose primary subject (surname) is NOT the Name Entity — see audit/schema-validation.json unmapped-scope note.

Phase 1C source verification found this generator does NOT read data/country-differentials.json despite that file's fields conceptually matching what it renders — it recomputes rank/movement directly from popularity.records-equivalent data every time. Under the canonical model, relationships.comparisonPairs[] would be the single computed/stored destination this generator both reads and (if precomputed) writes.

Must run after name pages exist per its own header comment — under the canonical model this ordering constraint would remain (an equivalent-name page still needs the anchor entity to exist), but 'name pages exist' becomes 'the canonical entity record exists' rather than a file-generation-order dependency.

Aggregation page — reads popularity.records[] across many entities. Distinct from generate-popularity-year-pages.js below (Phase 1A cataloged both as separate scripts covering an overlapping year range).
Aggregation pages — read popularity.records[] across many entities rather than domains of a single entity.
The one page-generator confirmed to actually read data/country-differentials.json (contrast with generate-compare-pages.js above).
A data-build script, not a page renderer — included because it is the producer half of the relationships.comparisonPairs[] canonical field.
Derives independently from data/popularity.json, in parallel with generate-country-differentials.js above rather than building on it — see audit/knowledge-redundancy.json.

The merge step every page-generator except generate-sibling-pages.js and the standalone generate-names-like.js currently benefits from. Under the canonical model this merge happens once, upstream of ALL generators, by construction — there is no 'enriched' vs 'base' file distinction left to accidentally skip.

generators.role: Data-build (writes data/origin-overrides.json, curated, top-300-name scope per its own header comment)
generators.note: The actual research-entry point for the origin domain today. Under the canonical model this remains the write-path for origin.* — the highest-leverage field per audit/knowledge-roi.json (Phase 1D).
Rule-based, deterministic — matches the schema's x-provenance: computed annotation for classification.categories[].
The sole entry point for real popularity research today.

generators.role: Data-build (Phase 1 acquisition Step 4 — meaning + origin enrichment from Wikidata/curated linguistic datasets)
canonicalFieldsRequired: writes: meaning.primary, meaning.confidence, origin.confidence, citations.sources[] (via its own meaning_source/origin_source/confidence_score output columns)
generators.note: Missed in this phase's first pass over audit/build-pipeline.json's generator catalog — added after audit/schema-validation.json's cross-check flagged the gap. Its own header comment states 'only verified meanings; store source reference; no AI-generated meanings,' meaning this script already intends to produce exactly the citations data the canonical model formalizes — but its meaning_source/origin_source/confidence_score output columns were found to be present-but-always-null in the live data/normalized-names.json (audit/knowledge-coverage.json), suggesting this script's enrichment step is not currently wired into the live build pipeline's data path. Not independently re-verified in this phase.
